FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
Regulatory signs state the rules for direction, lane use, turning, speed, and parking, and a red circle with a slash over a symbol always prohibits something such as a left turn, right turn, or U-turn [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
Speed limit signs post the fastest or slowest safe speed allowed, with the maximum written for ideal driving conditions [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
Drop below the posted maximum when rain, snow, or fog makes the road slippery or hard to see, and take a different route when a posted minimum is too fast for you [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
Lane control signs show where you may go or turn, using arrow symbols on roadside or overhead signs and sometimes white arrows painted on the pavement [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
No-passing signs mark stretches where passing is unsafe, starting at the zone sign itself, with passing areas set by sight distance and passing allowed only when safe; the matching pavement markings are detailed on handbook page forty-five [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A01
The blue emergency notification sign stands on both sides of every rail crossing with a railroad phone number and crossing ID for reporting stalled vehicles, broken signals, or any track hazard [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A01
A stop sign orders a full stop until crossing traffic and the crosswalk clear, halting first at any stop line and then edging to the sign or intersection edge before proceeding when safe [A01].
Why it matters: the stop line and the visibility point are two separate stops in one maneuver.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A01
A yield sign orders you to slow down and give the right of way to traffic in the intersection or road you are entering [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A01
The divided-highway sign means the road ahead splits, so steer around the island or barrier [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A01
A one-way sign means traffic flows only in the direction of its arrow [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A01
Do-not-enter signs mark openings you must not use, such as exit ramps, divided-road crossovers, and one-way stretches [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A01
A wrong-way sign means you turned into opposing traffic, so leave the traveled roadway, stop, and turn around as quickly and safely as you can [A01].
Why it matters: this is the only sign that tells you the mistake already happened.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A02
Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols and mostly diamond-shaped, telling you to slow down and stand ready to stop for a hazard ahead [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A02
An intersection or crossroad sign means another road crosses yours ahead, so watch carefully for traffic crossing your path [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A02
A signal-ahead sign on a faster road tells you to expect an intersection with a stoplight [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A02
A merging-traffic sign tells drivers on the main road to expect other vehicles blending into their lane [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A02
A two-way-traffic sign means you are leaving a one-way road for a two-way road, so keep to the right [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A02
A divided-highway-begins sign means two-way traffic is about to split around a center strip [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A02
A divided-highway-ends sign means the center strip is ending, so watch for oncoming vehicles [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A02
A horse-drawn-vehicle sign means slow-moving buggies may share the road, so cut your speed and pass gently [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A02
A lane-ends sign means two lanes are merging into one, with merging traffic yielding [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A02
A farm-machinery sign means slow equipment may share the road, so cut your speed and pass gently [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A02
A pedestrian-crossing sign means watching for everyone crossing on foot or wheels, including wheelchairs and low-speed micromobility devices, with details in the pedestrian-conveyance section covered later [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A02
A deer-crossing sign means deer may step onto the road nearby, so slow down and scan carefully [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A02
A hill sign warns every vehicle that the road drops ahead, so test your brakes before the descent [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A02
A T-intersection-ahead sign means your road ends, so get ready to turn left or right [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A02
A school-bus-stop-ahead sign means a bus will soon load or unload children nearby, so watch for children and stand ready to stop [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A02
A gradual-curve sign means the road bends gently ahead, so prepare for the direction change [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A02
A slippery-when-wet sign means the pavement ahead slicks over in rain, so slow down in wet weather [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A02
Chevron signs back up curve signs wherever a direction change needs extra emphasis [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F31 | anchor: A02
A ramp-speed sign posts the recommended speed for an exit ramp [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F32 | anchor: A02
An advance-school-crossing sign means a school area with a marked crossing is near, so watch for children there; this sign may be yellow [A02].
Why it matters: the yellow note is the exception to the fluorescent school-warning rule.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0009]

Misconceptions: a red circle with a slash always prohibits, while plain regulatory signs instruct; advance school crossing signs may be yellow despite the fluorescent school-warning rule; the divided-highway sign describes the road ahead rather than ordering you to divide.

Mnemonic: slash means stop doing it; diamonds warn, chevrons curve, cross traffic crosses; deer, buses, and children each get their own advance sign.

Glossary: regulatory (an enforceable rule sign); prohibition (a red-circle-slash ban such as no U-turn); crossroad (a road crossing yours); chevron (a sharp-alignment marker reinforcing a curve); ramp speed (the advised exit-ramp speed); cross traffic (vehicles crossing your path).

Dynamic facts: none in these pages; every sign meaning above is stable handbook knowledge with no date-variable or place-variable values.
